incidents.victim: 40+ Irish credit unions (and possibly UK members)
incidents.vector: Hackers exploited a vulnerability in the systems of software supplier Wellington IT, which provides mobile banking apps to credit unions in Ireland and Northern Ireland.
incidents.impact: Payment details of credit union members were accessed in early October but went unnoticed for six weeks; more than 40 breach notifications have been filed with Ireland's Data Protection Commission, with no confirmed fraud yet.

incidents.vector: Attackers operating in Simplified Chinese on China Standard Time used the open-source autonomous AI penetration-testing tool Cairn to discover and exploit an unpatched zero-day path-traversal flaw in an open-source medical imaging application.
incidents.impact: Amazon's Threat Intelligence team found the operator's exposed Cairn server and confirmed the AI agents achieved unauthorized shell access to a university server with minimal human direction after thousands of failed credential and exploit attempts.

incidents.vector: The group, already inside victim networks via a BeyondTrust Remote Support zero-day, used a custom Golang tool ("BONESAW") to exploit a new vCenter zero-day (CVE-2026-123890), hijacking SAML tokens to forge SSO administrator access.
incidents.impact: Mandiant/GTIG confirmed the vCenter zero-day is being actively exploited for credential theft, data exfiltration, and full environment compromise; CISA added it to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog and Broadcom has released patches with no workaround.

incidents.vector: An "AI-generated cyber campaign" using the publicly available AI hacking platform ARTEX disrupted the Commission's HR systems, first detected October 22.
incidents.impact: Payroll, leave requests, medical reimbursements, and translation services were taken offline for more than 10 days as a protective measure; no evidence of a broad staff data breach or ransom demand has been found, and the investigation remains open.

incidents.victim: Equinor and Skagerak Energi (Norwegian energy companies)
incidents.industry: Energy / Oil, gas and power utilities
incidents.vector: Two Norwegian energy companies disclosed cyberattacks on consecutive days affecting internal IT systems; Equinor's email system went down and both companies say production and operations were not disrupted.
incidents.impact: No evidence of data theft has been confirmed by either company; other Norwegian energy firms including Aker BP and Statkraft raised alert levels, and Norway's national security authority had already warned of a "high" cyber risk to businesses.

incidents.victim: Rocket Mortgage LLC and Mr. Cooper (Nationstar Mortgage)
incidents.vector: Repeated failures to implement multi-factor authentication and to report prior cybersecurity incidents to regulators within required timeframes, discovered across multiple incidents tied to both companies.
incidents.impact: NY DFS fined Rocket Mortgage and Mr. Cooper a combined $6.75 million for MFA and late-incident-reporting failures under the state's Cybersecurity Regulation (23 NYCRR Part 500).

incidents.victim: American and European victims of Southeast Asian scam compounds
incidents.vector: Scam-compound operators in Cambodia ran virtual-currency investment fraud schemes against Americans, protected by armed groups that provide security to the scam-center networks.
incidents.impact: Treasury's OFAC sanctioned scam-center operator Zhao Hui and two affiliated companies for facilitating cyber-enabled investment fraud targeting U.S. citizens.

incidents.victim: Cryptocurrency holders, gaming platform users, and VoIP software users in Europe
incidents.vector: Trojanized installers disguised as messaging and VoIP software, along with decoy financial documents, delivered a Go-based remote access trojan, a Python infostealer, and a cryptocurrency clipboard hijacker.
incidents.impact: Cisco Talos assessed with low confidence the campaign is linked to North Korean actors based on tooling overlap; the RAT uses Solana blockchain transaction memos to resiliently host its command-and-control addresses.

incidents.victim: Employees of a Silicon Valley technology and defense company (reportedly Palantir)
incidents.vector: A Russian national entered the U.S. illegally, used fraudulent identification and electronic tracking devices, and conducted in-person surveillance and stalking of company employees near their offices and homes.
incidents.impact: DOJ indicted Igor D'iu for acting as an unregistered Russian agent targeting a company supplying technology used by Ukraine; he faces up to 10 years in prison.

incidents.vector: Hackers gained unauthorized access to two of Japan's national supercomputers.
incidents.impact: Stolen data included registered-user details, research data from home directories, and SSH keys used to connect the supercomputers to outside services.

incidents.vector: Hackers breached a third-party vendor that provides SharePoint data-migration services to Infoblox and stole customer data from it.
incidents.impact: Cybersecurity firm Infoblox is notifying customers of the breach; the number of affected customers and whether extortion was involved have not been disclosed.

incidents.vector: Security breach of the ticketing platform's official website.
incidents.impact: Fandango notified customers and authorities of the October breach; scope of exposed data was not disclosed.

incidents.vector: Security breach disclosed by the Australian retail chain.
incidents.impact: Coles says no data has been confirmed stolen so far, though the company noted this could change as its investigation continues.

incidents.victim: At least 12 Dutch websites (sports and recreation sector)
incidents.vector: A malicious advertising partner served ads containing code designed to collect identifying data from older iPhone models.
incidents.impact: Affected sites warned users directly; most of the impacted properties are sports and recreation-related.

incidents.victim: 178+ organizations including CNN, BBC, Zoom, HSBC, Equifax, Salesforce, GitLab, and NPR
incidents.vector: A hacker exploited a vulnerability in the Optimizely web-experimentation platform to inject malicious JavaScript into customer accounts, which was then served from Optimizely's own CDN under its legitimate certificate.
incidents.impact: For about 16 hours, the injected script swapped cryptocurrency wallet addresses, skimmed payment card data, and attempted to deliver mobile exploit kits to visitors of at least 178 high-profile websites before Optimizely patched the flaw and removed the code.

incidents.vector: A cyberespionage campaign active since mid-2025 deploys custom remote access trojans via phishing and DLL sideloading, using covert HTTP/3 (QUIC) channels for command-and-control to evade network inspection.
incidents.impact: Unit 42 observed the group steadily refining two custom RAT families over nine months to maintain high-stealth, long-term intelligence collection access inside targeted government networks.

incidents.vector: A ransomware and data-extortion group claimed the attack, which forced the retailer to shut down online ordering and use alternative in-store transaction processing.
incidents.impact: Systems and the website were restored within the week; the company says no evidence yet shows customer financial data was stolen, and has not addressed the extortion group's leak-site claims.

incidents.victim: Semiconductor manufacturers, U.S. defense-policy organizations, and civil society groups (19 organizations)
incidents.vector: Chinese-speaking attackers paired the open-source Cairn AI penetration-testing framework with Chinese AI models to autonomously plan and execute 25 intrusion operations against 19 organizations.
incidents.impact: Unit 42 assessed with moderate confidence this is China-nexus intelligence collection; attackers gained unauthorized access or data at 10 of the targets, exposing over one million personal records at one organization, retrieving military and government identities, and modifying a live industry standards-ballot document.

incidents.victim: Supermarkets and medical facilities across France and 10+ other European countries
incidents.vector: Unidentified threat actors gained unauthorized access to refrigeration controllers and set them to defrost mode, raising unit temperatures as high as 50°C (122°F).
incidents.impact: A first wave hit roughly 700 French supermarkets overnight Oct. 11-12; a second wave overnight Nov. 1-2 expanded to 100-115 retail locations across 10+ additional countries and also affected medical-facility refrigeration, spoiling food inventory ahead of the holiday season with no confirmed blood-product losses.
